capabilities: Syncs notes, images, PDFs and other vault files between computer and Android
Encrypts file names and contents end-to-end with AES-256-GCM and verifies integrity with SHA-256
Resolves conflicts by writing a separate conflict copy instead of overwriting
Publishes selected folders to a read-only web viewer with private exclusions and revocable per-person links
Renders Markdown, wikilinks, embeds, backlinks and Bases views in the web viewer
extras: README is in Russian and the plugin is installed by copying files into the plugin folder, not from the community directory. Listed MVP limits: no server-side version history, access only through secret links (no accounts or e-mail), DataviewJS is not executed in the public viewer, deleted binary blocks are not cleaned up automatically, and very large media libraries need streaming publication.
problem: Users who want their vault kept in step across devices without handing file names or contents to a third-party server, and who also want a read-only web copy of chosen folders, have no built-in way to do it.

requires.name: Self-hosted sync server on a VPS (Docker)

summary: Self-hosted sync plugin that mirrors a vault between desktop and Android through an end-to-end encrypted server, plus a read-only web viewer.
